prompt.text:
Audrey Lake is the Chief Investment Officer of Mid States University Management Corporation (MSUMC), 
an endowment fund overseeing the university’s investment portfolio. MSUMC invests over half of its assets 
in equity securities, both public and private. As part of the equity review process, Lake has assigned the 
analyst team questions to consider. First, MSUMC’s Investment Office is more interested in being able to 
benefit from improved company performance than the seniority of claims when they invest. Second, 
MSUMC’s Investment Office seeks a “voice” in management decisions of the companies in which they 
invest. Third, MSUMC targets broad exposure across the equity universe, buying both publicly listed and 
private equities across company life-cycle stages. Finally, MSUMC has a very long investment horizon.
Which of the following securities has the lowest seniority on claiming cash flows from a portfolio company?

choices: Debt
Preference shares

Common shares
Feedback
Choice C is correct. Holders of common shares have the residual claim on a company’s cash flows and assets. 
Common shareholders are paid once all other claims are settled.
Choice A is incorrect as debtholders have the highest seniority in receiving cash flows relative to preference 
and common shareholders.
Choice B is incorrect as preference shareholders are senior to common shareholders.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text:
Which of the following provides the most correct response as to why MSUMC prefers investing in common 
shares rather than preference shares?

choices: Common shares typically provide higher dividends than are received from holding preference shares.

Common shares provide the opportunity to vote on corporate decisions in addition to the possibility for 
improved dividends or higher stock price as company performance improves.

Dividends on common shares are less uncertain because of the higher seniority of common shares’ 
payoffs.
Feedback
Choice B is correct. MSUMC’s stated goals of being able to capitalize on improvements and having a “voice” 
on corporate decisions best match the features of common shares.
Choice A is incorrect as common shares may have lower or higher dividends than preference shares.
Choice C is incorrect as common shares are less senior than preference shares.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text:
In which company life-cycle stage is MSUMC most likely to find both publicly listed and private company 
equities as investments?

choices: Start-up
Growth

Mature
Feedback
Choice C is correct. In the mature stage of the company life cycle, MSUMC is likely to find both publicly listed 
equity and private equity securities. Publicly listed companies are often mature stage companies, while buyout 
equity companies in private equity are often mature stage companies.
Choice A is incorrect as start-up companies are unlikely to qualify for public listing because of insufficient 
revenue and profitability.
Choice B is incorrect given that growth stage companies may not have achieved the profitability or other 
characteristics needed for public listing.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text:
MSUMC’s long investment horizon is most relevant to which one of the following equity market features in 
their decision to allocate between publicly listed and private equities?

choices: Owner–manager separation versus overlap
Standardized disclosures versus limited disclosures

Liquidity versus illiquidity of shares
Feedback
Choice C is correct. MSUMC’s long investment horizon allows them to consider holding illiquid private shares if 
they earn, on average, a higher return than public share holdings.
Choice A is incorrect as this feature is more relevant to MSUMC if they want to be able to exert greater 
management control through equity ownership, and it is independent of MSUMC’s investment horizon.
Choice B is incorrect as the disclosure requirements are also independent of MSUMC’s investment horizon.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text: Participating preference shares are least likely to entitle the shareholders to participate in:

choices: corporate decisions through voting rights.
additional distribution of the company’s assets upon liquidation.

additional dividends if the company’s profits exceed a predetermined level.
Feedback: 
Correct. Participating preference shares do not entitle the shareholders to participate in corporate decisions 
through voting rights. But they do entitle them to (1) an additional dividend if the company’s profits exceed a 
prespecified level and (2) additional distribution of the company’s assets upon liquidation, above the par.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text:
A company has issued only one class of common shares, and it does not pay dividends on them. It has 
also issued two types of non-cumulative preference shares: one that is putable and the other callable. 
Which of these securities will most likely offer the lowest expected return to the investor?

choices: Common shares
Putable preference shares

Callable preference shares
Feedback: 
B is correct. Putable preference shares are less risky than their callable counterparts. They give the investor 
the option to put the shares back to the company. Because of the lower risk, they will provide a lower expected 
rate of return. Common shares are the most risky, whether or not they are dividend paying, and are likely to 
offer the highest expected return.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text: Preference shares are less risky than common shares because preference shares have:

choices: fixed dividends.
a guaranteed return if a company is liquidated.

a larger portion of total return based on future price return.
Feedback: 
A correct because dividends on preference shares are known and fixed, and they account for a large portion of 
the preference shares’ total return. Therefore, there is less uncertainty about future cash flows.

feedback.neutral: Refer to official CFA curriculum for detailed solution explanation.

prompt.text:
Firms with which of the following characteristics are most likely candidates for a management buyout 
(MBO)?

choices: Firms with low levels of cash flow
Firms with high dividend payout ratios

Firms with large amounts of undervalued assets
 Feedback: 
C is correct. Companies with large amounts of undervalued assets (which can be sold to reduce debt) that 
generate high levels of cash flow (which are used to make interest and principal payments on the debt) are 
likely candidates for MBO transactions
